definitions.explanation: A part of speech in grammar that connects words, phrases, clauses, or sentences. In Japanese grammar, conjunctions appear at the beginning of a sentence or clause to link it logically to the previous one.

examples.japanese: 「⟦しかし→しかし：00986_shikashi⟧」⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{接続詞|せつぞくし}だ。
{接続詞|せつぞくし}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{使|つか}う→使う：00473_tsukau⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{文章|ぶんしょう}→文章：02957_bunshou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧つながり⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{良|よ}く→良い：02350_yoi⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧。
examples.english: Using conjunctions improves the flow between sentences.

examples.japanese: ⟦{日本語|にほんご}→日本語：00614_nihongo⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{接続詞|せつぞくし}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、{順接|じゅんせつ}・{逆接|ぎゃくせつ}・⟦{並列|へいれつ}→並列：08417_heiretsu⟧⟦など→〜など：03095_nado⟧⟦{様々|さまざま}→様々：01559_samazama⟧な⟦{種類|しゅるい}→種類：01560_shurui⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: Japanese conjunctions come in various types, such as consequential, adversative, and parallel.

notes:
USAGE:
A grammatical term used in language education and linguistics. Japanese conjunctions (such as ⟦しかし→しかし：00986_shikashi⟧, だ⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧, ⟦それ→それ：00994_sore⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧, ⟦ところ→ところ：01137_tokoro⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧) typically appear at the start of a new sentence, unlike English conjunctions which can appear mid-sentence. This is an important distinction for learners.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {接続詞|せつぞくし}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{使|つか}う→使う：00473_tsukau⟧ (to use a conjunction)
- {順接|じゅんせつ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{接続詞|せつぞくし} (consequential conjunction, e.g., だ⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧)
- {逆接|ぎゃくせつ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{接続詞|せつぞくし} (adversative conjunction, e.g., ⟦しかし→しかし：00986_shikashi⟧)

RELATED WORDS:
- ⟦{接続助詞|せつぞくじょし}→接続助詞：26609_setsuzokujoshi⟧: conjunctive particle — a particle that connects clauses within a sentence (e.g., ～⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で, ～て⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧)
- ⟦{品詞|ひんし}→品詞：16086_hinshi⟧: part of speech — the broader category to which conjunctions belong
